description: The pie chart shows the distribution of emotion categories across utterances in the IEMOCAP dataset, with a total of six slices representing distinct affective labels. The slices are labeled and color-coded as follows: Frustration in light blue at approximately 25.1%, Neutral in dark blue at approximately 23.1%, Excitement in red at approximately 14.1%, Sadness in orange at approximately 14.7%, Anger in yellow at approximately 14.9%, and Happiness in medium blue at approximately 8.1%. Percentage values are printed inside the slices, and the category names are placed around the outside of the pie; no separate legend is shown and no slice appears exploded or otherwise visually emphasized. The slices appear arranged roughly from larger to smaller segments around the chart, with the smallest segment corresponding to Happiness.
caption_used: Distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, illustrating the relative prevalence of affective states across utterances. The pie chart comprises six distinct emotional categories: Frustration (25.1%), Neutral (23.1%), Happiness (8.1%), Anger (14.9%), Sadness (14.7%), and Excitement (18.5%). Frustration remains the dominant emotional category, while Happiness and Excitement exhibit a notable disparity, with Excitement consistently surpassing Happiness by a substantial margin. The data reveal that negative emotions, such as Frustration and Anger, collectively account for nearly half of the recorded utterances, underscoring their prominence in the dataset. Percentages are displayed with respect to the total number of utterances, and the slices are arranged in descending order of magnitude, beginning with Frustration.
